newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher, with the long term future slightly off its new record high and the 10-year cash spread over Bunds was at a record low.
"The end of the day triggered a wave of stop-losses buying before the weekend," a dealer in Madrid said.
"But the only things which seems to be sure is that Spanish market will continue to be very strong," he added.

The peseta jumped to end at 83.46/3.49 versus the mark, from 84.09/11 at Thursday's close. It hit levels not seen since May, soaring through a key level earlier in the session after the Bank of Spain stopped selling pesetas, dealers said.
"I don't think the peseta's strength can force the Bank of Spain to cut rates but for sure, it can become a factor," said Gregorio Gomez at All Trading in Madrid.
The Bank of Portugal's repo rate cut by 20 basis points to 6.50 percent was also be seen supporting Spanish bonos, dealers added.
The yield curve continued to steepen, dealers said.
The previous record low in the the spread over German Bunds was on January 3, and the long-term future contract hit its previous peak at 112.86 on December 31.
